note: No rule of the Cook Islands' Financial Supervisory Commission or of the banks together fixing an account number's form was read, and no national clearing code was found. ANZ Cook Islands, the bank the game's Cook Islands account is held at, says on its own contact page (read 2026-10-30) that a customer receiving a payment from overseas gives the sender their six-digit account number as it appears on their ANZ account or statement, with ANZ's SWIFT code (ANZBCKCR) and its BSB, 01-0975, beside it. So the number is written as ANZ's six digits; the BSB is the bank's and branch's code given beside the number for payments from overseas, not part of it, and isn't in Payments NZ's register of New Zealand branches (read the same day, no 01-0975). Readings to check: this is one bank's own number, not a national rule; the Bank of the Cook Islands (whose page gives its own BSB, 05-1501) and BSP number their accounts in forms not read, so a payee there may not fit. No check digit is published.

sources.title: ANZ Cook Islands, Contact us (Receiving overseas payments)
sources.said: To receive an inward payment from overseas, ... you'll need to provide the sender with: ... Your six-digit account number (as it appears on your ANZ account/statement) ... The ANZ SWIFT code, which is ‘ANZBCKCR’ ... The ANZ BSB number, which is ‘01-0975'
